§53 divides a PER-DECADE rate (6.2277e-05 per decade of r_max) by a PER-RUNG TOTAL (8.060e-03). A rung is NOT a decade: J3(nq_r=60) -> J4(nq_r=72) moves the reach 5062.1 -> 7269.9, i.e. 0.157197 decades. On §53's OWN coefficient the commensurable term is 9.7898e-06 and the separation is ×823, not ×130. `6.22e-5` vs `8.06e-3` IS NOT A COMMENSURABLE PAIR

AND the coefficient is fitted at r_max >= 1e6 while the ladder truncates at r = 7270. The MEASURED rate in the band containing that radius is 9.5734e-03/decade -- 154× larger than §53's. Across a rung the truncation term is between 5.212e-05 and 1.505e-03 (log-interpolated at r=7270: 4.462e-04), so the separation is between ×5.4 and ×155, central ×18. ×130 sits at the FAR END of that bracket -- it is what you get using the rate measured at r in [1e4,1e5], i.e. BEYOND the grid's own truncation radius. At the radius the ladder actually truncates the separation is ONE order, not two

RULING: FALSE AS ARITHMETIC, UPHELD IN PART AS A MAGNITUDE. The printed pair `6.22e-5` (per decade of r_max, fitted at r >= 1e6) against `8.06e-3` (per rung, at r ~ 7.3e3) is not commensurable in units OR in radius; taken at face value it gives ×823. Repaired at the truncation radius the central separation is ×18 -- one order, not two -- and ×130 is recoverable only from a rate measured outside the grid. The two errors push in OPPOSITE directions, which is why the number looked plausible. The CONCLUSION -- §52's truncation does not account for §51's under-claim -- SURVIVES, on a margin roughly 6-7× thinner than advertised
